policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders an imperative continuing the imperative of the first clause: "Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ." A future indicative (base ἀναπληρώσετε) would appear as "and so ye shall fulfil"; the bare "fulfil" coordinated with "Bear ye" answers to the aorist imperative ἀναπληρώσατε.
The unit is only the order of φρεναπατᾷ and ἑαυτόν; both readings say the same thing and English word order ("he deceiveth himself") is fixed by its own grammar. No ASV note is mapped here.
ἐὰν and ἂν are alternate forms of the same generalizing particle in the relative clause; "whatsoever a man soweth" renders either identically. Nothing in the ASV or its notes distinguishes them.
ἐγκακῶμεν and ἐκκακῶμεν are orthographic variants of one verb with the same sense; "let us not be weary" renders either. No ASV note is mapped here.

Indicative ἔχομεν and subjunctive ἔχωμεν after ὡς καιρὸν both come into English as "as we have opportunity"; the ASV shows no distinguishing marker. The mapped note "Or, while" is classed alternative_rendering and concerns the English rendering of ὡς, so it cannot decide the reading.

This unit and the μὴ of v008 are the same negative in different positions relative to τῷ σταυρῷ; either arrangement yields "only that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ." The ASV's only mapped note is an alternative_rendering for "for" and does not touch the negative.
ASV reads "the cross of Christ" with no "Jesus"; the added Ἰησοῦ of r01 would be represented in so literal a version, and no note records it.

The negative is present in both readings of the verse — retained here in the base, carried by the ἵνα μὴ of r01 at v006 — so the ASV's "that they may not be persecuted" is satisfied either way and does not fix its position.

ASV's text has the present "they who receive circumcision" (περιτεμνόμενοι) and relegates the perfect to a mapped textual_variant note, "Some ancient authorities read have been circumcised," which is exactly r01 περιτετμημένοι. Text over margin selects the base.

The unit is the presence of the article with κόσμῳ; English requires "the world" in either case, and the mapped note "Or, whom" is an alternative_rendering about δι' οὗ. Nothing distinguishes the readings.
ASV begins "For neither is circumcision anything" with no rendering of ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ; r01's "for in Christ Jesus neither..." would show in the English and does not.

ASV "neither is circumcision anything" renders the copula ἐστιν; ἰσχύει would give "availeth" (as in the versions that print it). The mapped note "Or, creation" concerns καινὴ κτίσις and is an alternative_rendering.
ASV reads "the marks of Jesus" with no "Lord"; the added κυρίου of r01 would appear as "the Lord Jesus" and no note records it.
